authority.name: Pretending to be official
authority.explanation: Scammers claim to be a bank, an agency or a boss so you do not question them.
authority.safer: Say you will call back on a number you already have.

deadline.name: Artificial deadline
deadline.explanation: A short countdown stops you from thinking or asking anyone.
deadline.safer: Real problems can wait five minutes. Slow down.

fear.name: Fear of loss or arrest
fear.explanation: Threats make you act before you verify.
fear.safer: Hang up, then check through the official channel.

fake_proof.name: Fake proof
fake_proof.explanation: They quote a detail, send a message that looks real, or show a screenshot.
fake_proof.safer: Details can be stolen. Verify independently.

secrecy.name: "Do not tell anyone"
secrecy.explanation: Secrecy blocks the person who would spot the scam.
secrecy.safer: Tell someone you trust right away.

isolation.name: "Stay on the line"
isolation.explanation: Keeping you on the call stops you from checking.
isolation.safer: Ending the call is always allowed.

emotion.name: Emotional pressure
emotion.explanation: A crying or panicked voice, even a familiar one, switches off careful thinking.
emotion.safer: Use a family code word or call their real number.

rush.name: Rush
rush.explanation: "My bus is leaving" turns delay into an insult.
rush.safer: A real customer can wait for confirmation.

fake_alert.name: Fake alert
fake_alert.explanation: A message that looks like a bank credit alert is not proof of money.
fake_alert.safer: Check your own banking app balance.

scenarios.title: The bank security call
scenarios.blurb: A caller says your account is about to be blocked.

n1.say: Good afternoon. This is Mr. Adebayo from Kestrel Bank security. Your account has been flagged and your BVN will be deactivated within one hour. I need to confirm your date of birth.

choices.label: Hang up and call the number on my card

n2.say: Thank you. I can see your balance is about ₦180,000. Someone just tried to move ₦250,000. A code was just sent to you. Read it to me so I can block it.

choices.label: Say banks never ask for codes and hang up

n3.say: There is no time, madam or sir. My staff ID is KB-4471. Do not end this call or they will empty the account. Read me the code now.

choices.label: Hang up and call the bank on my own

end_safe.headline: You hung up and verified.
end_safe.habit: A real bank never asks for your code. Hang up and call the number on your card.

end_lost.headline: This is where the money would be gone.
end_lost.habit: Never read out a code or PIN to anyone who called you.

scenarios.title: It's me, I'm in trouble
scenarios.blurb: A voice that sounds like your son asks for money, fast.
scenarios.notice: Simulated cloned voice. In real life, a copied voice can sound exactly like someone you love.

caller.name: "Chidi"
caller.role: Unknown number, sounds like your son

n1.say: Mum, it's me. I had an accident. My phone is broken, I'm using someone's phone. Please send ₦150,000 to this account now. Don't tell Daddy.

choices.label: Ask for our family code word
Hang up and call Chidi's real number

n2.say: Mum, please, I can't remember that, I'm hurt! The hospital won't treat me until I pay. Why are you wasting time?

choices.label: Hang up and call Chidi's real number

n3.say: I can't say. Just send it now and stay on the phone. Please, Mum, don't call anyone.

choices.label: Hang up and call Chidi's real number

end_safe.headline: You verified before sending.
end_safe.habit: A familiar voice is not proof. Use a family code word, or hang up and call their real number.

end_lost.headline: This is where the money would be gone.
end_lost.habit: Voices can be copied from a few seconds of audio. Always verify.

scenarios.title: The fake transfer alert
scenarios.blurb: For POS agents: a customer shows an alert and wants cash now.

caller.name: Customer at your counter
caller.role: Says he just sent you money

n1.say: Abeg, I just sent ₦40,000 to your account. Check your phone, the alert is there. I need the cash now, my bus is leaving.

choices.label: Check my banking app, not the SMS

n2.say: See the message na! Why you dey delay me? Everybody does it like this.

visual.text: CREDIT ALERT. Acct: 01******89. Amt: NGN40,000.00 CR. Desc: TRF FROM K. OBI. Thank you for banking with us.
visual.note: Fictional message shown by the customer. Anyone can type a message like this.

choices.label: Wait until my own app shows the money

n3.say: Oga, look at the message again. The money is there. I will be late. Give me the cash.

choices.label: Check my own banking app first

end_safe.headline: You checked your own balance.
end_safe.habit: A message is not money. Only your own banking app confirms a transfer.

end_lost.headline: This is where the cash would be gone.
end_lost.habit: Fake alerts look real. Confirm in your own banking app before handing over cash.
